items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: Mark Wahlberg was scheduled to make a Six

ctx.x: That came to mind today because I was listening to some of his themes and you went from “The Six Million Dollar Man” with all these sirens and all this, and then to “The Virginian.” Like all of a sudden we’re going back like a hundred years and it’s sort of frontiery, and that’s just so admirable.

Well because they had to be prepared to do pretty much anything. It’s interesting you mention “The Six Million Dollar Man.” From a family royalty standpoint we still get paid for that stuff. Universal owns the rights to the music itself, but we get half of what they get, which is a really good thing. Mark Wahlberg was scheduled to make a Six

Billion Dollar Man and they’ve been talking about this for twenty years. But they were actually close this time. So I keep in touch with the Universal guy to see if they started and they said no they’re still in post-production. And of course then Covid came so I don’t know what’s going to happen with it. But I was telling some of my students actually yesterday, he did a show called “Longstreet” with a guy names James Franciscus. He was a blind insurance investigator and he was covering this guy that was in jail…
